newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: One of Cambodia's ruling parties in new alliance.
newsitem.headline: One of Cambodia's ruling parties in new alliance.

text.p: The Cambodian People's Party (CPP) on Wednesday recruited a third small party to an alliance set up in response to a front established by its main rival in the country's coalition government.

Second Prime Minister Hun Sen of the CPP and Prum Neakareach of Moulinaka, the smallest party in the 120-member parliament with one seat, signed an agreement at a ceremony attended by top officials from both sides in the CPP headquarters.
The CPP has signed agreements with two other groups, the Liberal Democratic Party and Information Minister Ieng Mouly's wing of the divided Buddhist Liberal Democratic Party (BLDP).
These alliances followed an announcement last month by Hun Sen's rival, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh of the royalist FUNCINPEC, that he would set up a pre-election alliance.

Political analysts believe Cambodia's two main coalition parties are marshalling their forces ahead of local and general polls due in 1997 and 1998 and have warned that pre-election alliances could exacerbate their strained relations.
Hun Sen turned down an invitation to join Ranariddh's alliance, which groups FUNCINPEC with the officially unrecognised opposition Khmer Nation Party and the BLDP wing headed by Ieng Mouly's rivals.
Both sides, which formed an uneasy partnership after U.N.-run general elections in 1993, have denied the alliances were aimed at each other.

But ties between the two have deteriorated in the past year due to FUNCINPEC demands for more power to reflect their narrow 1993 victory at the polls and efforts by both premiers to win allegiance from thousands of rebel Khmer Rouge defectors.
Hun Sen said on Wednesday that the coalition government was still working.
